title: The Clue Outside the Picture
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript:
Suppose a computer programme appears unusually good at identifying a plant disease from photographs. Before celebrating, we should ask what information it has actually learned to use. A photograph contains much more than the leaf at its centre. The background, the camera settings and even a label at the edge may be associated with the answer in a collection of training images.

In a teaching example, a group of students built a classifier using photographs supplied by two greenhouses. Most diseased plants had been photographed at the first greenhouse on a dark workbench. Most healthy plants had been photographed at the second greenhouse against a pale wall. When images were divided randomly into training and test groups, the programme seemed highly accurate.

The instructor then asked the students to photograph healthy and diseased leaves against the opposite backgrounds. Performance fell sharply. Covering the background also changed many predictions, even though the visible symptoms on the leaves were left untouched. The system had discovered a convenient association that would not remain reliable outside the original collection.

To improve the evaluation, the class separated images by greenhouse rather than distributing pictures from both locations across every group. This made the test harder, but it better represented the challenge of using the programme at a new site. They also collected examples in which health status and background were no longer closely linked.

The case illustrates a general problem in machine learning. A successful test may measure the ability to recognise the circumstances of data collection rather than the phenomenon we care about. Removing misleading clues can help, but evaluation must also reflect the conditions in which a system will operate. Otherwise, an apparently impressive result may offer little practical assurance.

questions.prompt: What unintended clue was available in the training photographs?
options: The time printed in the students’ notebooks.
The number of leaves on plants outside the frame.
The language spoken by the greenhouse staff.
The association between background and plant health.
questions.answer: The association between background and plant health.
questions.explanation: 患病和健康植物主要来自不同温室，分别配深浅背景，背景与答案形成错误关联。

questions.prompt: What happened when plants were photographed against the opposite backgrounds?
options: The programme became more accurate on every image.
It stopped detecting the edges of photographs.
The symptoms on the leaves disappeared.
questions.explanation: 调换背景后表现大幅下降，说明程序依赖了不可靠的背景线索。

questions.prompt: Why did the class separate test images by greenhouse?
options: To better simulate use at a location not represented in training.
To ensure that every test photograph came from the same camera.
To remove all diseased plants from the evaluation.
To make the test results easier to predict.
questions.answer: To better simulate use at a location not represented in training.
questions.explanation: 按温室分组可更贴近在新地点部署时面对的挑战。

questions.prompt: What is the speaker’s main warning?
options: More photographs always reduce prediction accuracy.
Backgrounds must be identical in every practical application.
A high test score may reflect data-collection clues rather than useful understanding.
Computer programmes cannot process photographs of living things.
questions.answer: A high test score may reflect data-collection clues rather than useful understanding.
questions.explanation: 高测试分数可能只是识别了采集条件，而没有掌握真正要判断的现象。
